subject.title: TUI /sessions list: gateway-injected inbound metadata block used as session title (shows 'untrusted metadata' for all sessions)

question: Should maintainers replace the stale conflicting fork PR with a narrow maintainer-controlled fix, or ask the fork author to refresh it first?
rationale: The bug is source-proven and narrow, but an open fork PR still uses closing syntax while current labels ask ClawSweeper not to create a duplicate fix PR automatically.

options.title: Replace with narrow same-repo fix
options.body: Open or adopt a maintainer-controlled PR that strips inbound metadata in title extraction and threads resolved display fields through both title hydration paths, then close the stale fork once replacement exists.

options.title: Ask fork author to refresh
options.body: Keep the fork PR as the candidate only if the author rebases it against current main, resolves conflicts, and supplies real TUI/session-list behavior proof.

options.title: Wait for broader title work
options.body: Leave this bug open until broader derived-title product work lands, accepting continued metadata leakage in the TUI/session-list path meanwhile.

recommendation.title: Replace with narrow same-repo fix
recommendation.body: Open or adopt a maintainer-controlled PR that strips inbound metadata in title extraction and threads resolved display fields through both title hydration paths, then close the stale fork once replacement exists.

likelyOwner.reason: Recent gateway session-list history and prior title-path commits make steipete the best available owner for choosing the repair route.
